elena (design): quick thread — trying to settle on validation patterns for the billing address form. inline errors vs top summary, and how we show required fields. thoughts? elena (design): current mock uses inline errors that appear on blur, plus a summary at top if there are multiple errors. wondering if that's overkill. sam (frontend): inline-on-blur is nice for UX, but we need a11y hook. screen readers won't necessarily jump to the inline message unless we focus it or use aria-live. jax (a11y): agree. prefer a top error summary with link-to-field for keyboard users + inline errors that are announced. pattern: focus moves to the summary on submit, then user can tab to fields. mina (product): main use case is quick checkout — we don't want extra friction. inline errors for single fields, but summary when submit fails with >1 error? seems reasonable. tyler (qa): watch out for raced validations. if we do async postcode validation, the error might show after submit summary — flakey. need consistent timing. sam (frontend): implementation note — we can do this: show inline on blur, but on final submit, if any errors exist show a summary with role="alert" and focus it. also add `aria-describedby` from input -> message. jax (a11y): example snippet that works: ```
2 errors found. Press enter to go to first.
Address is required ``` Focus summary on submit so NVDA/JAWS read it. remy (engineering-manager): what's our stance on required-field indicators? * vs explicit label like "(required)" — designers often prefer asterisk but a11y folks prefer explicit text. elena (design): asterisk is visually lighter but ambiguous. I'd prefer visible "Required" label for long forms, or tooltip help. For short forms, * might be fine. jax (a11y): asterisk alone isn't accessible unless you have hidden text for screen readers. If we do *, add `required`. That keeps visuals but communicates to SR. sam (frontend): agree, will add sr-only. also need to ensure required fields are in DOM order before optional ones? not necessary but grouping helps. mina (product): last item: destructive actions — for deleting saved cards we currently show a two-button modal. debate was typed-confirmation vs simple confirm+undo. high security customers want typed confirmation for card deletion? remy (engineering-manager): typed confirmation adds time; for deleting payment methods maybe typed confirmation or 2-step: modal + snackbar undo. tyler (qa): typed-confirmation reduces accidental deletes in tests too — but increases support tickets when users mistype. We should reserve typed-confirm only for account-level destructive ops (delete account, remove billing owner). ela­na (design): (typo) — meant elena: for saved cards i'd vote modal + undo. typed-confirm for "Delete organization". jax (a11y): ensure modal focuses on heading and trap focus. typed-confirmation fields should have clear labels and accessible error states. mina (product): resolution proposal: - Inline errors on blur for fields + aria-describedby. - On submit, if any errors, focus a summarized role=alert that links to fields. - Required fields: show * visually + sr-only "required" text. - Destructive actions: typed confirmation only for org-level or billing-owner changes; modal+undo for saved payment instruments. elena (design): love that. can someone add copy suggestions for the summary and the typed-confirm flows? sam (frontend): I'll prototype the pattern and push a small PR with markup and a11y attributes. will include a story in storybook. tyler (qa): I'll add test cases: keyboard-only nav, screen reader read order, async validation race. jax (a11y): I'll review the PR for screen reader behavior and color contrast on error text. form-bot: Reminder: design review scheduled Thu 10am. mina (product): ok thanks — will mark this as the working pattern and include in the forms styleguide doc. :thumbsup:
